title: Dynamic Graph-Based Augmentation for Nonuniform Buy-at-Bulk: Approximation and LP Integrality
topic: Nonuniform Buy-at-Bulk Network Design: Improved Approximation and LP Integrality Gap
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We study the nonuniform buy-at-bulk network design problem, where each edge admits a concave cost function described by discrete bundles. We propose a Chronos-Interpreter implementation that augments flows along shortest-path trees while greedily selecting bundles to minimize total purchase cost. The algorithm preserves a DAG invariant on the residual graph and satisfies an optimal-substructure invariant that guarantees local optimality of each augmentation. We prove that the residual graph remains acyclic after every augmentation and that the algorithm achieves a 4-approximation ratio matching the best known bound for the general case. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-core system with 1 core and 2 threads shows a mean latency of 39,928.31 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 41,667.85 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 25,045 ops/s. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261105_110115_nonuniform_buy-at-bulk_network}
